legend: A succinate dehydrogenase–deficient renal cell carcinoma composed of bland cells with eosinophilic (but not oncocytic) cytoplasm is seen. Intracytoplasmic inclusions containing eosinophilic, flocculent, or pale material are a common and distinctive feature.

The SDH complex comprises two anchoring subunits, SDHC and SDHD; the catalytic components SDHA and SDHB; and SDHAF2, which is responsible for flavination of the SDHA component of the complex. If any component of the SDH complex is lost, the complex becomes dysfunctional and SDHB immunohistochemistry becomes negative.

A succinate dehydrogenase–deficient renal cell carcinoma composed of bland cells with eosinophilic (but not oncocytic) cytoplasm is seen. Intracytoplasmic inclusions containing eosinophilic, flocculent, or pale material are a common and distinctive feature.

diagnosis: Pulmonary chondroma arising in Carney triad
legend: In contrast to pulmonary hamartoma, the pulmonary chondromas associated with Carney triad do not show entrapped respiratory epithelium between the lobules of cartilage and do not contain other mesenchymal elements, such as fat, smooth muscle, or myxoid spindle cells.

diagnosis: Pulmonary chondroma arising in Carney triad
legend: In contrast to pulmonary hamartoma, pulmonary chondroma associated with Carney triad shows a smooth contour, lacking invaginations of entrapped respiratory epithelium between cartilage.
copyright: Jennifer M. Boland, Division of Anatomic Pathology, May Clinic, Rochester MN

legend: Immunohistochemistry for SDHB is not always easy to interpret. In this paraganglioma, associated with germline mutation, there is a diffuse cytoplasmic blush in all the neoplastic cells. As this staining contrasts with the intense granular expression in non-neoplastic internal controls, the tumour is still considered succinate dehydrogenase deficient.

Immunohistochemistry for SDHB in a succinate dehydrogenase–deficient gastrointestinal stromal tumour is shown. There is no expression of SDHB in any of the neoplastic cells. The granular cytoplasmic expression in the non-neoplastic cells, which acts as an internal positive control, is emphasized.

Morphological clues to succinate dehydrogenase–deficient paragangliomas are inconsistent but include well-developed, almost circular, nests of epithelioid cells sometimes with pale or vacuolated cytoplasm {2417}.

This phaeochromocytoma, not associated with SDH mutation, demonstrates diffuse strong SDHB expression. The cytoplasmic and distinctly granular (mitochondrial) pattern of expression is noted (SDHB immunohistochemistry).
Succinate dehydrogenase–deficient GIST commonly demonstrates a multilobulated or plexiform growth pattern.
Succinate dehydrogenase–deficient GIST is usually epithelioid or epithelioid predominant. Sometimes the epithelioid cells demonstrate a vaguely nested architecture.

diagnosis: Succinate dehydrogenase–deficient pituitary neuroendocrine tumour (PitNET) / pituitary adenoma
legend: This succinate dehydrogenase–deficient PitNET is indistinguishable morphologically from a sporadic tumour.

diagnosis: Imaging of paragangliomas in familial paraganglioma syndrome
legend: Multiple para-aortic and pelvic paragangliomas are identified with 68Ga-DOTATATE PET-CT in a patient with a pathogenic germline SDHB mutation.

Immunohistochemistry for SDHB may be difficult to interpret. In this case the weak cytoplasmic blush in the neoplastic cells contrasts markedly with the strong granular expression in the internal controls. This tumour should be considered succinate dehydrogenase deficient.
